examples.trans: Let us go from here, my dear, before we catch it.

examples.text: Немедленно дай эту коробку сюда мне.
examples.trans: Give that box here to me immediately.

examples.text: Ты зачем вообще сюда сегодня приехала?
examples.trans: Why on earth did you come here today?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'all', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Вот этот отель весь принадлежит ей!
examples.trans: This entire hotel belongs to her!

examples.text: Нет, не слишком, ведь это инвестиция.
examples.trans: No, not too much, because it is an investment.

examples.text: Ах ты бессовестный негодяй, я тебя убью!
examples.trans: Oh you shameless scoundrel, I will kill you!

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'чего').

examples.text: Нечего тебе отрываться от нашего коллектива!
examples.trans: There is no reason for you to separate yourself from our team!

examples.text: Мне терять нечего.
examples.trans: I have nothing to lose.

examples.text: Тут нечего делать.
examples.trans: There is nothing to do here.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'рываться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to break away / separate oneself'.

related.gloss: not to to break away (negated infinitive)

examples.text: Нечего тебе отрываться от нашего коллектива!
examples.trans: There is no reason for you to separate yourself from our team!

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и отрываться вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and to break away on time.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'our', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Нечего тебе отрываться от нашего коллектива!
examples.trans: There is no reason for you to separate yourself from our team!

examples.text: Наша Катя уже совсем взрослая девочка.
examples.trans: Our Katya is already a completely grown-up girl.

examples.text: Ребята, а где сейчас наша Катя?
examples.trans: Guys, and where is our Katya right now?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'collective, staff, team' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Нечего тебе отрываться от нашего коллектива!
examples.trans: There is no reason for you to separate yourself from our team!

examples.text: Это меня коллектив заставил.
examples.trans: The staff forced me into this.

examples.text: У нас на работе очень дружный коллектив.
examples.trans: We have a very friendly team at work.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'money' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: А на следующий день он страховку оформил.
examples.trans: And the very next day he took out an insurance policy.

examples.text: А сегодня последний день этой моей страховки.
examples.trans: And today is the very last day of this insurance of mine.

examples.text: Если палец будет сломан, я получу деньги.
examples.trans: If my finger is broken, I will get money.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Сеня, ты чего там вдруг завис?
examples.trans: Senya, why did you freeze up over there?

examples.text: Я четыре года назад порезал себе палец.
examples.trans: Four years ago I cut my finger.

examples.text: И за четыре года нет ни одной царапины.
examples.trans: And in four years he has not had a single scratch.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'then, afterwards', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Деньги за зеркало я тебе потом отдам.
examples.trans: I will pay you back for the mirror later.

examples.text: Слушай, попробуй потереть палец на тёрке.
examples.trans: Listen, try grating your finger on the grater.

examples.text: Сначала кофе, потом работа.
examples.trans: First coffee, then work.

meanings.en: to give away, to hand over
meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'дать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will give', paired with 'отдавать'.

examples.text: Деньги за зеркало я тебе потом отдам.
examples.trans: I will pay you back for the mirror later.

examples.text: То есть я отдам деньги и выйду в ноль?
examples.trans: So I give you the money and break even?

examples.text: Ну что, доченька, ты уже отдала заказ?
examples.trans: Well, sweetheart, did you already deliver the order?

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Ладно, шеф, я никому не скажу.
examples.trans: Fine, chef, I will not tell anyone.

examples.text: Ладно, давай двадцать тысяч, и по рукам.
examples.trans: Fine, make it twenty thousand, and we have a deal.

examples.text: Ладно, признаюсь честно, она сейчас в душе.
examples.trans: Fine, I admit it honestly, she is in the shower right now.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'anyone', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ладно, шеф, я никому не скажу.
examples.trans: Fine, chef, I will not tell anyone.

examples.text: Я же вчера сказал, больше никаких встреч.
examples.trans: I told you yesterday, no more meetings.

examples.text: А мне, стало быть, близкий родственник.
examples.trans: And to me, therefore, a close relative.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Шеф, вы не хотите мне палец сломать?
examples.trans: Chef, would you like to break my finger?

examples.text: Не будешь работать, я тебе спину сломаю!
examples.trans: If you do not work, I will break your back!

examples.text: И за четыре года нет ни одной царапины.
examples.trans: And in four years he has not had a single scratch.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will say', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.text: Я же вчера сказал, больше никаких встреч.
examples.trans: I told you yesterday, no more meetings.

examples.text: Что ты сказал?
examples.trans: What did you say?

examples.text: Скажите, где метро?
examples.trans: Excuse me, where's the metro?
